brief: Lead's brief: JS-039 sat at 68, behind every open task, depending on JS-037 (29, in Refine/Spec). No OIDC exists. Options: keep 68 (A); 30, directly after the identity tasks (B); 36, after the household and capacity set (C); split off a first slice (D). How many households run an identity provider is unverified: no dogfood or issue data either way.
tradeoff: A delays nobody, but single sign-on arrives after stages 4 to 6 of a road that puts it in stage 3. Every household with a provider keeps a second password per viewer, and its operator keeps accounts by hand in two places, indefinitely. B gives those households sign-on one task after Quick Connect, but the household set (30 onward) waits one build longer, and that set has a waiting household behind it (D-056) where OIDC has none. C gives it about six tasks later than B, and delays nothing a viewer is waiting on. JS-056 and the tasks at 37 to 46 (GPU, preset, autoscaling signal, measurement) each wait one build longer, a cost to operators. D has no slice worth a viewer's time: web sign-in without the TV code leaves an OIDC viewer with no password and no way onto a TV, so the smallest useful slice is both criteria, which is the whole task. Given up under C: households with a provider wait through the household and capacity set, and operators wait one build longer for example sizes and what follows.
entry: JS-039 moves from 68 to 36, after JS-178. JS-056 moves to 37, and the tasks at 37 to 46 each move down one. B is rejected because the household set has a waiting household and OIDC has only the promise. A is rejected because last place puts a stage 3 promise behind stages 4 to 6 with no data to justify it. D is rejected, and JS-039 is not split. Its criteria stay the two it has, with its own guessing bound (note of 2026-11-19) and no cookie (invariant 63). Provider groups, several providers and account provisioning rules do not enter it; each needs a household asking. Reopens on: a household with an identity provider waiting to move in, or an issue from one (JS-039 goes to 30, option B); the dogfood read of D-072 showing a viewer stalled or refused (capacity goes ahead, D-073); JS-037's Refine showing the TV code cannot serve an account without a password (JS-039's second criterion is priced in a brief before JS-037 builds).
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Signing in is easy and safe. A password, a code entered on the TV from a phone, or the household's own single sign-on'; road stage 3, 'People: accounts, sign-in by code and single sign-on', ahead of stages 4 to 6. Owner, 2026-11-20: a request alone is not evidence of need. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product. D-056, D-073.
